note: Employers whose public job postings come in as jobs (scripts/ingest/run.mjs postings). One line per employer: the name its board goes by, the company exactly as our data names it (and, in also, other companies we list under their own names whose factories the same board hires for), the hiring system and the board's token or address. An employer that is not read says why under leftOut. The employers are read in the order they are listed: boards that cost one request first, Workday's last and smallest first, so that a platform that turns the run away costs the fewest employers. scripts/ingest/postings/registry.mjs --check holds this file to its shape. Nothing behind SmartRecruiters' API is listed: its robots file disallows it. A Workday board that could not be read from the machine that verified it is left out, with its address, until a person adds its line: the workflow reads only the registry's lines.

employers.note: The board is Andersen's and Renewal by Andersen's together: its retail and installation postings name places with no factory and wait.
The career site is mostly H-E-B's stores: only postings at a place where we list a factory become jobs.
Honeywell's aerospace business has a board of its own; its factories are filed under Honeywell.
Its careers page also embeds an hourly portal (hourlyjobs-reynoldsconsumerproducts.icims.com); the all-jobs portal is the one read.
Novolex took over Pactiv Evergreen in 2025; our factories are still filed under Pactiv Evergreen's name (Temple among them).
The parent's portal; its subsidiaries have portals of their own, not read.
One career site for the whole of HII: Newport News Shipbuilding and Ingalls Shipbuilding are rows of their own, and each posting is filed under the company whose factory it is at.
One career site for the Volvo Group worldwide: Volvo Trucks North America and Mack Trucks are rows of their own. Volvo's cars are another company and are not named.

One career site for PACCAR: Peterbilt is a row of its own. The row named PACCAR Inc. is not named: its three factories are Trico Industries' (Torrance and Odessa) and a Kenworth dealer's (San Antonio), which this board does not hire for; Kenworth's own factories (Chillicothe, Renton) and PACCAR's engine factory (Columbus, Mississippi) are not in our data, and postings there wait.
About 1,900 postings worldwide, 25 to a page: some 80 requests for the listing.

General Electric is not named: that row also holds factories that are not GE Aerospace's. The board names its sites by their town alone and says no state; sites writes out the towns where we list a factory of GE Aerospace, GE Aviation Systems or GE Engine Services (Evendale is the village GE Aerospace Evendale, 1 Neumann Way, stands in), and the other towns wait in the run's report until a person writes them out.
The company row named Micron holds other firms' factories (Micron Industries, Micron Manufacturing): the chip maker is Micron Technology.
RTX has no factory under its own name: Raytheon, Collins Aerospace and Pratt & Whitney are recorded as parts of it, and their factories are used. Pratt & Whitney Engine Services is a row of its own.
